title: Study of volasertib and vinorelbine in children and adolescents with relapsed/refractory or progressive tumors – Ein Herz für Kinder INFORM2 VolVin
official: INFORM2 exploratory multinational, multi-arm phase I/II basket trial of volasertib and vinorelbine in children and adolescents with relapsed/refractory or progressive tumors [INFORM2-VolVin]
summary: Main objective: The aim of this trial is to determine the combination dose, safety and preliminary activity of the combination treatment with volasertib and vinorelbine applying an intra-individual dose escalation concept in order to achieve the optimal dose in terms of safety and activity.

interventions.name: Navirel 10 mg/ml Konzentrat zur Herstellung einer Infusionslösung

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Children and adolescents with: - Arm A:  PRC1 high expressing (H score ≥ 100) by IHC refractory/relapsed/progressive molecularly confirmed EwS - Arm B:  MYC(N)-amplified, contrast-enhancing, refractory/relapsed/progressive MB who have previously received craniospinal irradiation OR  refractory/relapsed/progressive NB -	Arm C: Refractory/relapsed/progressive RMS - Arm D: Newly diagnosed H3K27 altered DMG (incl. DIPG)
2. For NB patients only: Disease that is measurable as defined by RECIST v1.1 OR metaiodobenzylguanidine (MIBG) avid bone marrow involvement with:  - An unequivocally new MIBG avid osteomedullary site OR - A relative MIBG score ≥ 1.2
3. Adequate hematologic and organ function within 14 days prior to initiation of treatment, as defined by the following:	 Hematology:            	Absolute granulocytes	≥1.5×109/l (unsupported) 	Platelets	≥100×109/l & stable 	Hemoglobin	≥8g/dl or ≥4.96mmol/L & stable Biochemistry:	Total bilirubin	≤1.5 × upper limit of normal (ULN) 	AST (SGOT)	≤3×ULN 	ALT (SGPT)	≤3×ULN 	Serum creatinine	≤1.5×ULN
4. Electrocardiogram (ECG): normal QTc interval QTcF ≤440ms
5. Ability of patient and/or legal representative(s) to understand the character and individual consequences of the clinical trial
6. Females of childbearing potential must have a negative serum or urine pregnancy test within 72 hours prior to initiation of treatment
7. Sexually active women of childbearing potential must, provided that in compliance with national legislation, agree to use acceptable and appropriate contraception during the study and for at least 7 months after the last study treatment administration
8. Sexually active male patients must, provided that in compliance with national legislation, agree to use a condom during the study and for at least 180 days after the last study treatment administration
9. Absence of any psychological, familial, sociological or geographical condition potentially hampering compliance with the study protocol and follow-up schedule; those conditions should be discussed with the patient before registration in the trial
10. Before patient screening and registration, written informed consent, also concerning data and blood/tissue transfer, must be given according to International Conference on Harmonization of Technical Requirements for Registration of Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH)/ Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and national/local regulations.
11. Time between biopsy/puncture/resection of the current refractory/relapsed/progressive tumor (Arm D: newly diagnosed) and registration ≤ 24 weeks. In patients receiving therapy not impacting biomarker stratification, time between biopsy/puncture/resection of the current refractory/relapsed/progressive tumor and registration of ≤ 36 weeks is allowed
12. Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) material for IHC PRC1 expression analysis submitted
13. Molecular analysis (including PRC1 mRNA expression) for biomarker identification in laboratories complying with DIN EN ISO/IEC 17025 or similar via INFORM molecular diagnostic platform or equivalently valid molecular pipeline
14. In case molecular analysis was not performed via INFORM Registry molecular pipeline: transfer of molecular data (DNA and RNA sequencing)
15. No standard of care treatment available (except Arm D where SOC radiotherapy is included).
16. Age at the time of signing informed consent ≥ two to ≤ 21 years
17. Life expectancy > 3 months, sufficient general condition score (Lansky scale ≥ 70 or Karnofsky scale ≥ 70). Transient states like infections can be accepted, and also stable disabilities resulting from disease/surgery (hemiparesis, amputations etc.) can be accepted and will not be considered for Lansky/Karnofsky assessments
18. Disease that is measurable as defined by RAPNO criteria or RECIST v1.1 (as appropriate) according to the central review
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients with CNS tumors or metastases who are neurologically unstable despite adequate treatment (e.g. convulsions)
2. Patient is financially dependent on the sponsor, investigator or trial site
3. Participation in other ongoing clinical trials
4. Previous treatment with a PLK1 inhibitor
5. Previous participation in this clinical trial.
6. Presence of any of the following contraindications or medical conditions precluding study treatment: clinically significant, uncontrolled heart disease; known hypersensitivity to vinorelbine, other vinca alkaloids, or any of the excipients of the study medication; concomitant administration of yellow fever vaccine; severe hepatic impairment unrelated to the underlying malignancy; severe active infection or a history of severe infection within the preceding two weeksAny anticancer therapy (e.g., chemotherapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapy, biological response modifiers, endocrine anticancer therapy, bevacizumab) within two weeks or at least five half-lives (whichever is longer) of study drug administration
7. Any anticancer therapy (e.g., chemotherapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapy, biological response modifiers, endocrine anticancer therapy, bevacizumab) within two weeks or at least five half-lives (whichever is longer) of study drug administration
8. Major surgery within 21 days of the first dose. Gastrostomy, ventriculo-peritoneal shunt, endoscopic ventriculostomy, tumor biopsy and insertion of central venous access devices are not considered major surgery, but for these procedures, a 48-hour interval must be maintained before the first dose of an investigational drug is administered
9. Current treatment with strong P-glycoprotein/ CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors other than those allowed per Section 5.8.1. Medications that are substrates of P-glycoprotein or CYP3A4 are allowed but should be used with caution
10. Traditional herbal medicines; these therapies are not fully studied and their use may result in unanticipated drug-drug interactions that may cause or confound the assessment of toxicity. As part of the enrollment/informed consent procedures, the patient will be counseled on the risk of interactions with other agents, and what to do if new medications need to be prescribed or if the patient is considering a new over-the-counter medicine or herbal product. For information on CYP substrates and P-glycoprotein inhibitors or inducers see Section 5.8.1
11. Presence of underlying medical condition (e.g. gastrointestinal disorders or electrolyte disturbances) that in the opinion of the Investigator or sponsor could adversely affect the ability of the subject to comply with or tolerate study procedures and/or study therapy
12. Pregnant or lactating females
13. Patient is held in an institution by legal or official order
